primary_object_card.object_statement: A v1 finite predictive object is the state-relabeling-invariant exact uniform-start distribution of binary words through length eight generated by a minimal strongly connected four-state rational unifilar process; independent lossy views and a supervised learner may predict this frozen equivalence on unseen objects but cannot define or certify it.
primary_object_card.plain_language_definition: Two hidden finite machines count as the same bounded object only when their exact probabilities agree for every binary word from length one through eight under the frozen uniform-start convention. The learner sees only independently corrupted trajectories. It may predict signatures and retrieve another view of an unseen object, while Julia exact rational verification remains the semantic authority.

source_anchors.quote_or_summary: Freezes the process family, independent lossy views, learner, controls, every-seed gates, three-engine roles, and literal claim ceilings.
Freezes v0 exclusions, exact signatures, disjoint splits, and full-observation-horizon-matched test pairs without sealing learner source or reporting learned test metrics.
Independently reconstructs retrieval, predictive JS, matched-pair decisions, controls, and every frozen primary gate from raw PyTorch outputs.

native_terms.finite predictive object: An equivalence class with identical exact uniform-start word probabilities through frozen length eight.
native_terms.unseen object: A test-split predictive equivalence class excluded from training and validation object sets.
native_terms.semantic owner: Julia independently verifies exact rational finite semantics and arbitrates disagreement; learned embeddings have no semantic authority.
native_terms.scoped PyTorch learner: The fixed GRU and DeepSets model used for supervised prediction, retrieval, and frozen controls in this benchmark, not a claim about all PyTorch capabilities.
